_note: Real answers from `claude -p` (Sonnet, Nov 2026), recorded with the app's prompts. moveExplanation/positionPlan/bestMoves(Pt): Ruy Lopez after 5...Be7. gameReview/gameReviewPt: the third mock game (English / Brazilian Portuguese). Used by the browser mock backend.

moveExplanation.summary: 5...Be7 is a good, solid move. It's the main Closed Ruy Lopez move, and the engine sees the position as about equal after it.
ideas: The bishop on e7 develops a piece and protects the e5 pawn's support. It also clears the way for Black to castle kingside.
It guards against tricks on the e-file. If White plays Re1, Black can answer with ...b5 and ...O-O, as in the engine's main line.
The engine slightly preferred 5...Nxe4, the Open Variation. That's a sharper path, and Be7 is just as good for equality.
moveExplanation.plan_next: Black should meet 6.Re1 with ...b5, then play ...Bb7 or ...O-O after the bishop retreats to b3. Castle soon, and get the d-pawn to d6 to support e5. After that, bring the pieces out with ...Re8 and ...Bb7.

positionPlan.summary: The position is about equal. It's a normal Closed Ruy Lopez and you're still in book. Your e4 pawn is attacked by the Nf6 and isn't defended, so deal with that first.
positionPlan.phase_focus: Finish development, protect the e4 pawn and keep a solid center while Black still hasn't castled.
plan: Play Re1 to defend e4 and put the rook on the open-looking e-file.
Follow with c3 and d4 (or d3) to build a strong center.
Retreat the bishop to b3 if Black plays ...b5, then think about a4 to challenge the queenside.
opponent_ideas: Black wants to play ...b5 to kick your bishop, then castle and play ...d6.
Black may take on e4 with ...Nxe4 if you leave the pawn undefended.

candidate_moves.idea: Best move: defends e4 with a rook, develops a piece and keeps the main Ruy Lopez structure.
Solid alternative: defends e4 with a pawn and keeps a flexible, safe setup, though it blocks your c1 bishop a little.
Trades your bishop for the knight and doubles Black's pawns, but gives up your strong bishop pair. It's playable and about equal, though less ambitious.

answer.summary: You played a solid Queen's Gambit opening and won by resignation. The middle of the game was messy. You gave away a pawn with 15.b4, but your opponent's blunder 22...g5 swung the game to you. You missed the cleanest follow-up with 23.Qxb7, but your opponent erred again and you converted the win well.

lessons.title: Check hanging pieces before pushing pawns
lessons.explanation: With 15.b4 you let your opponent take a pawn and drop your knight-capture idea. 15.Qxe4 simply won the knight back first. Always ask what is attacked before making a side move.

lessons.title: Look for the strongest capture, not the greediest
lessons.explanation: After 22...g5 you were winning. 23.Rxa8 kept everything protected and kept the pressure on. 23.Qxb7 won a bishop but let your opponent back into the game. When ahead, choose the safest strong move.

lessons.title: Trade rooks and queens when ahead
lessons.explanation: Once you were up material, you traded pieces and kept your king safe. Your opponent resigned after the queen trade on d6. This simple technique makes wins easier.

key_moments.comment: 15.b4 pushed a pawn when your knight on e4 had just been exchanged. Your opponent could take it with 15...Bxb4, and you lost the pawn without compensation. Recapturing first was cleaner.
Your opponent moved the queen to h5 and gave up some of the advantage. Bringing the knight to c5 was more active and kept the pressure on.
22...g5 was a big blunder that loosened the king and left the bishop on b7 and the knight on d7 hanging. It turned a roughly equal game into one that was close to winning for you.
23.Qxb7 won a bishop, but it was not the cleanest move. Taking on a8 first kept the pressure on and avoided counterplay. You were still much better.
23...Qg6 was another blunder that left you up material and winning. Your opponent could have put up more resistance with 23...Nc5.

answer.summary: Você teve uma boa abertura, mas errou com 15.b4? e ficou em desvantagem por um tempo. Seu oponente devolveu a vantagem com 22...g5?? e 23...Qg6??, e você converteu o final com segurança até a desistência dele.

lessons.title: Cuidado ao empurrar peões com peças soltas
lessons.explanation: Com 15.b4? você deixou a posição frouxa e acabou perdendo material. Antes de avançar um peão, veja se ele deixa algo sem defesa. Era melhor 15.Qxe4.

lessons.title: Priorize a melhor captura ou troca
lessons.explanation: No lance 23, 23.Qxb7?? jogou fora parte da vantagem. 23.Rxa8 era mais forte e mantinha o controle. Examine todas as capturas antes de escolher.

lessons.title: Continue pressionando e espere os erros
lessons.explanation: Seu oponente cometeu erros graves com 22...g5?? e 23...Qg6??. Você se manteve ativo e aproveitou, depois converteu o final com calma.

key_moments.comment: 15.b4? deixou você pior, de cerca de 50% para 38%. Capturar o cavalo com a dama era melhor e mantinha a posição equilibrada.
18...Qh5?! deu ao oponente uma posição menos boa. 18...Nc5 desenvolvia o cavalo e mantinha mais pressão.
22...g5?? foi um erro grave e enfraqueceu o rei do oponente. Você passou a ter grande vantagem.
23.Qxb7?? permitiu ao oponente recuperar chances. Tomar a torre com 23.Rxa8 era mais forte.
23...Qg6?? foi outro erro grave e devolveu a vantagem a você. 23...Nc5 era a defesa mais resistente.

bestMoves.summary: All three moves are about equal, so this is a choice of style. 6.Re1 and 6.d3 keep the Ruy Lopez tension and lead to a slow, strategic game. 6.Bxc6 gives up the bishop pair to wreck Black's pawns, and it is a bit less ambitious.

moves.idea: Defends the e4 pawn, which is currently attacked and undefended. It puts the rook behind the center and prepares d4 and c3 in the main Closed Ruy Lopez setup.
moves.plan: After ...b5, retreat with Bb3, then play a4 to hit Black's queenside. Follow with d3 and Bd2, and later c3 and a central break. Keep your pieces active and your king safe.

moves.idea: Defends e4 with a pawn and keeps a solid, flexible structure. It opens the c1-bishop and avoids early tension in the center.
moves.plan: After ...b5, play Bb3, then a4 to challenge Black's queenside. Next come c3, Bc2 and Nbd2 to bring the knight toward f1 or g3. Re1 can follow later.

moves.idea: Trades your bishop for the knight to double Black's c-pawns. It also removes a defender of e5 and gives you a simple structural target.
moves.plan: After ...dxc6, play d3 and then h3 and a4 to keep things under control. Bring your knight to c3 and aim for a small, steady edge. Black has the bishop pair and an easy game, so don't expect much more than equality.

bestMoves.recommendation: I'd suggest 6.Re1. It is the engine's top move, and it solves the e4 problem in the most natural way, with a rook on a useful file. It is the main line, so it's easy to learn and repeat. 6.d3 is just as good and a little simpler if you want fewer things to remember.

bestMovesPt.summary: As três jogadas são praticamente equivalentes: o jogo está equilibrado em todas. 6.Re1 e 6.d3 mantêm a tensão e levam à Ruy Lopez clássica; 6.Bxc6 simplifica e dá um jogo mais calmo e menos teórico.

moves.idea: Defende o peão e4 com a torre e prepara d3 e c3 mantendo uma pressão sólida no centro. É o plano principal da Ruy Lopez fechada.
moves.plan: Após ...b5, jogue Bb3, depois a4 para atacar o flanco da dama das pretas, e d3 para apoiar o centro. Desenvolva o bispo para d2 e mantenha as peças bem coordenadas.

moves.idea: Protege o peão e4 com um peão e constrói um centro firme e simples, sem gastar tempo com a torre.
moves.plan: Depois de ...b5 e Bb3, jogue a4 e c3, e leve o bispo para c2. Mais tarde, prepare Nbd2 e Re1 com um jogo de manobras lento.

moves.idea: Troca o bispo pelo cavalo para dobrar os peões pretos em c6 e tirar a tensão do flanco da dama. Em troca, você entrega o par de bispos.
moves.plan: Jogue d3, depois h3 e a4, e Nc3 para desenvolver as peças. Procure uma posição estável, sabendo que a vantagem estrutural é pequena.

bestMovesPt.recommendation: Eu sugiro 6.Re1, o melhor lance do motor. Ele protege e4, segue o plano padrão da abertura e é fácil de entender: desenvolver, pressionar o centro e depois jogar Bb3, a4 e d3. 6.d3 também é ótimo e igualmente simples, se você preferir um centro sólido de peões.

openingOverview.summary: The Closed Ruy Lopez is a classic opening where White builds slowly and keeps pressure on the e5 pawn and the knight on c6, while Black develops safely and aims for a solid position. Players choose it because it is sound, rich in plans, and gives long-term chances without early risks. The engine says it is about equal, and the explorer shows White scoring a healthy 56% at master level, mostly through draws.
openingOverview.pawn_structure: Both sides have pawns on e4 and e5, so the center is locked in tension. White's main idea is to support e4 (with Re1 and d3 or c3 and d4) and later break with d4. Black wants to protect e5 with ...d6, kick the bishop with ...b5, and later free the position with ...d5 or ...Na5 and ...c5. The e4 pawn is currently only defended by nothing but the Nf3 trick, so White must watch it: it is attacked by the Nf6 and is undefended.
plans_white: Play Re1 to defend e4 (85% of master games, scoring 56%). Then c3 and d4 to claim the center.
Keep the bishop on the diagonal with Bb3 after Black's ...b5, and add Nbd2 and Nf1-g3 to reposition the knights.
Build slowly with d3 and c3 if you prefer a safer, solid game (6.d3 also scores 56%).
plans_black: Play ...b5 to kick the bishop, then ...d6 and ...O-O to get castled and safe.
Support e5 with ...d6 and ...Bb7 or ...Bd7, keeping the center solid.
Free your game later with a pawn break such as ...d5 or ...c5 once you are fully developed.

traps.name: The e4 pawn trick
traps.description: Right now e4 is only attacked, not defended. If White forgets it and plays something slow, Black can take on e4 with the knight. Play Re1 (or d3) so the pawn is safe. As Black, 5...Nxe4 is only good when White cannot punish it, so check carefully before grabbing.

traps.name: Taking on c6 too early
traps.description: After 6.Bxc6 dxc6, White's idea is to win e5. But Black usually can defend and gets the bishop pair, so grabbing the pawn with Nxe5 can lose material to tactics on the e-file. Make sure e5 is truly winning before you take it.

traps.name: Ignoring the pin on the e-file
traps.description: After Re1 and Black's careless ...b5 or ...O-O moves, the e5 pawn can become loose if the knight on c6 leaves or is traded. Watch for Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 ideas.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to defend e4 before playing other moves, so the pawn is lost to ...Nxe4.
Retreating the bishop to the wrong place after ...b5: Bb3 keeps it active, while giving it up on c6 without a reason hands Black the bishop pair.
As Black, rushing pawn breaks like ...d5 before castling and finishing development, or forgetting to castle.
openingOverview.middlegame: Expect a slow, maneuvering fight. White usually gets a small space edge and prepares d4, while Black stays solid and waits for a good moment to hit back in the center. Improve your worst-placed piece, such as a knight heading toward f1-g3 or d2-f1, and keep your king safe. Do not rush: patience is rewarded here.

openingOverviewPt.summary: A Ruy Lopez Fechada é uma das aberturas mais clássicas e respeitadas: as Brancas desenvolvem rápido, rocam e pressionam o cavalo de c6, que defende o peão e5. Nos jogos de mestres, 6.Re1 aparece em 85% das partidas e as Brancas pontuam 56%, mostrando que é uma posição sólida, com leve vantagem de iniciativa e pouco risco.
openingOverviewPt.pawn_structure: Os dois lados têm peões centrais e4 e e5 frente a frente, e o centro costuma ficar fechado por muito tempo. As Brancas querem preparar c3 e d4 para abrir o centro com apoio; as Pretas querem manter e5 firme, jogar ...b5 e ...d6 e depois ...O-O, atacando a base com ...d5 ou ...f5 em algum momento. Por enquanto o peão e4 está atacado e sem defesa extra, então 6.Re1 é a forma natural de protegê-lo.
plans_white: Defender e4 com Re1 (a jogada mais popular e a preferida do motor), retirar o bispo para b3 depois de ...b5 e preparar c3 e d4.
Jogar c3 e d4 para ganhar espaço no centro e dar ao bispo de b3 uma diagonal ativa contra f7.
Reagrupar as peças (Nbd2-f1-g3 ou Bd2/Nc3) e usar o ataque ao centro e à ala do rei se as Pretas ficarem passivas.
plans_black: Jogar ...b5 para expulsar o bispo, depois ...O-O, ...d6 e ...Bb7 para desenvolver com solidez.
Manter o peão e5 bem protegido e preparar o avanço ...d5 para igualar no centro.
Reagrupar o cavalo de c6 (por exemplo ...Na5 e ...c5) para ganhar espaço na ala da dama.

traps.name: Peão e4 sem defesa
traps.description: Se as Brancas fazem uma jogada lenta e esquecem de defender e4, as Pretas podem capturá-lo com ...Nxe4, pois o peão está atacado e não defendido. Com 6.Re1 (ou 6.d3) o problema desaparece.

traps.name: Bxc6 e captura em e5
traps.description: Se as Pretas ignoram a ameaça, Bxc6 seguido de Nxe5 ganha um peão. Por isso o cavalo de c6 e o peão e5 precisam estar sempre bem defendidos antes de qualquer jogada ousada.

traps.name: Ruim para as Pretas: ...b5 sem cuidado
traps.description: Depois de ...b5 as Pretas enfraquecem casas da ala da dama, e o bispo em b3 mira f7. Se esquecerem de roque ou desenvolvimento, as Brancas podem criar ameaças táticas contra f7.

common_mistakes: Não defender e4 e perder o peão central logo no início.
Trocar Bxc6 cedo demais sem um plano claro, entregando o par de bispos sem vantagem concreta.
Mover as mesmas peças várias vezes e esquecer de terminar o desenvolvimento antes de avançar peões na ala.
openingOverviewPt.middlegame: O jogo costuma ser manobrístico e posicional: ninguém precisa ter pressa. Melhore suas peças piores, mantenha o centro protegido e só abra a posição com c3 e d4 (Brancas) ou ...d5 (Pretas) quando suas peças estiverem prontas. Fique atento a táticas em f7 e e5 e a trocas que simplifiquem a favor de quem tem a melhor estrutura.
